1.why: All eight screens are static single-column cards with no animations, carousels, or pop-up overlays.

2.why: Each step has one bold heading and one filled dark-blue primary button that visually dominates, though the black 'Logs' panel competes for attention and the success message in step 2 is small green text.

3.why: Each screen presents a single field and a single action, so the needed control is quick to locate, but the dense privacy/simulation notice blocks on step 1 and the raw log panel add scanning overhead.

4.why: Steps are presented one at a time, but the user must carry the 32-character recovery token and the 6-digit MFA code from the log panel into input fields, and remember the unlisted 12-character password rule while typing.

5.why: No password manager hint, autofill affordance, 'remember me' checkbox, show-password toggle, or paste helper appears anywhere in the flow.

6.why: Nothing is saved or recognizable — the only pre-filled values (email in step 2, token in step 3) come from the current session, with no saved-item cues, masked account hints, or device recognition.

7.why: Sentences are short and high-contrast dark text on white, though step 1's two stacked notices about 'privacy-neutral' token simulation are abstract and jargon-heavy for a 67-year-old user.

8.why: No error state is shown in any of the eight screenshots — there is no invalid-token, wrong-code, or weak-password message describing a problem and its fix.

9.why: Only the password rule is described in prose ('at least 12 characters with uppercase, lowercase, a number, and a symbol'); no input placeholders, format examples, or sample email/token/code formats are given.

10.why: The flow offers only one authentication path (password plus emailed code) — there is no visible choice of biometric/face login, passkey, or alternative code delivery to compare.

11.why: Every screen shows exactly one input and one button, so the user is never faced with competing options.

12.why: Each action produces a confirmation (green 'recovery instructions will be sent', log entries, 'appointment request has been confirmed'), but some outcomes are only visible as technical log lines rather than plain user-facing messages.

13.why: There are brief inline instructions per step, but no tooltips, help links, contact-support option, or progress indicator explaining what the new step involves or how many remain.

14.why: No 'Back', 'Resend code', 'Start over', or 'Cancel' control appears on any screen, so recovering from a mistyped token or code is not visibly supported.

15.why: All eight screens reuse the identical header, card layout, label-above-field pattern, button style, log panel, and safety footer.
